key_insight: Machine-learning-driven Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics shows that Al content controls whether (MoCrTi)100−xAlx alloys order in one or two stages, with B2-type chemical ordering strongly boosting stiffness.
engineering_relevance: The results indicate that tuning composition and ordering can non-monotonically improve elastic properties, helping design refractory high-entropy alloys for high-temperature structural use.
method: Temperature-dependent thermodynamics, short-range order, and elastic constant analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports heat capacities and short-range order parameters that reveal single or double order-disorder transitions, along with compositional trends in elastic constants and moduli.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the accuracy and transferability of the machine-learning potential and on simulations, so experimental validation is still needed for real alloy processing conditions.
paper_title: Study of ordering in (MoCrTi)$_{100-x}$Al$_x$ refractory high-entropy alloys using machine learning interatomic potential
